brief:
Brief for team TS3012 (based on meetings 1-3)

Where we stand going into the final meeting (decided)
- We are building a universal remote for young consumers (under forty), not a TV-only one for everybody. [TS3012b: "I think we should go for universal, because apparently we're a separate company making separate c remote controls to sell to a lot of diverse people."] [TS3012b: "This is a new product and with this new product we want to appeal to younger people, which are um the younger people were defined under forty."]
- Case: rubber, in the company's yellow, with the leaner shape (square base, rounded top) Mark chose in meeting c. It runs on regular batteries. [TS3012c: "Okay, so we're definitely going for rubber."] [TS3012c: "I think we should th then take it take yellow."] [TS3012c: "Okay, will just take regular batteries."]
- Interface: the deluxe edition with an LCD screen, no scroll wheel (voted out), and a beep plus flash so a lost remote can be found. [TS3012c: "Yeah, I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."] [TS3012c: "No r no scroll-wheel. Okay. Um I don't see anything missing really."] [TS3012b: "We could make a combination that it goes beep and that you that some light lights up."]
- Inside: the advanced chip (the LCD screen needs it) and rubber push-buttons, because a rubber case only takes rubber buttons. [TS3012c: "The chip is advanced because we have the advanced features."] [TS3012c: "Okay, and if we use rubber, I already mentioned that, we can only use rubber buttons."]
- Targets from the kick-off still apply: selling price 25 Euros, production cost about 12.50 Euros. [TS3012a: "What do we This Quick What we're going to Selling price, twenty five Euros."]

What changed along the way
- LCD screen: dropped in meeting b as too big, power-hungry and costly, then brought back in meeting c because users want it (deluxe edition). [TS3012b: "I think we should lose the L_C_D_ screen, like you said."] [TS3012c: "Yeah, I think we'll I think we're going towards the deluxe edition anyway, because that seems to be what the people want."]
- Speech recognition: ruled out by Mark in meeting b (too hard across countries and languages), reopened in meeting c once a small speech component turned up and Dirk reported that over sixty percent of target users want it. By the end of meeting c it was drawn into the design (microphone next to the transmitter) but never explicitly confirmed, and it has not been costed. [TS3012b: "So I think implementing speech recognition is such a small um apparatus, it's very hard to do."] [TS3012c: "So we can implement it. So why why if it's small and we can imp why shouldn't we?"] [TS3012c: "Um where do we want the microphone, for example, to be?"]
- Power: the rechargeable unit and charging base discussed in meeting b gave way to a normal battery in meeting c. [TS3012c: "Yeah, but I think this rules out our unit our rechargeable unit."] [TS3012c: "Okay, will just take regular batteries."]
- Changeable covers: welcomed in meeting b, then pushed out of the basic design to 'maybe later'; wood was ruled out at the same time. [TS3012c: "But I think the basic thing let's just rule out wood for now and continue."] [TS3012c: "uh for example it's just something you can click on it like uh that's but it's not som not apparently that's not something we're working with in the basic design."]

Open actions and owners
- Nick (B, user interface) and Xavier (C, industrial design): work out the final design together, inside and outside, and bring the drawing to the meeting. [TS3012c: "Anyway, um apparently you guys, you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design."] [TS3012c: "You doodle a doodle us a nice nice design for for the next meeting, we'll be done."]
- Dirk (D, marketing): look up the exact survey figure on voice-recognition interest, do the market analysis, and find out what people are willing to pay above 25 Euros. [TS3012c: "Uh I'm I have to look it up."] [TS3012c: "was that you're uh we're gonna work on our own because you're gonna do the market market uh analysing I'm supposed to do the little work on the year-end report."] [TS3012b: "Maybe yeah, or maybe you can find out i what people are willing to pay."]
- Xavier (C, industrial design): still owes cost figures (none found yet, only that the LCD needs the more expensive advanced chip), and whether the remote can open the TV's own menu. [TS3012c: "I have no I still don't have any finance information, but at least we have a lot more to go on now"] [TS3012c: "Uh I only know that if we are using that, we need ano uh an advanced chip in it."] [TS3012b: "I think so uh we need to put some research into that if if we can open the menu, I think it's possible, just the way how to."]
- Mark (A, project manager): the final project report. [TS3012c: "was that you're uh we're gonna work on our own because you're gonna do the market market uh analysing I'm supposed to do the little work on the year-end report."]

Still disputed: settle these first
- Budget risk: nobody has costed the design. Nick warned in meeting b that with an LCD the remote cannot sell for 25 Euros; the LCD forces the more expensive advanced chip and speech recognition adds its own component. Expect to cut something once the cost sheet arrives. [TS3012b: "Oh, we're not going to be able to sell it for twenty-five then, with an L_C_D_ screen."] [TS3012c: "Yeah, we should too bad we don't have the finance."]
- Speech recognition: confirm whether it stays once the costs are known, and if it does, whether the remote should also talk back (Xavier raised it, Nick doubted it is needed). [TS3012c: "Yeah, but do you actually need the remote talking back?"]
- Shape: the working shape is Nick's design with the top rounded off, as Mark asked (it 'looks leaner'). Still open is the cost: Nick said smoothing the edges adds expense, and more curves cost more. Mark's wish for a rounder, fruit-like form was left to the covers, because Nick warned it follows one seasonal trend.
